skill.name: stockpulse
skill.description: Review manually entered SKU inventory, reorder thresholds, stock exposure, and estimated gross margin for small sellers.
skill.summary: Prioritize replenishment using manual SKU data, reorder thresholds, inventory cost values, and estimated gross margins.
skill.author: falconprojectai-arch

security_audit.summary: Static analysis reported no findings, so no finding verdicts were required. The reviewed skill describes manual inventory calculations and replenishment prioritization. No evidence found of prompt injection, data exfiltration, or unauthorized actions in the supplied skill.

content.value_statement: Small sellers need to identify low stock and understand the cost of inventory from manually maintained records. StockPulse guides inventory validation, reorder prioritization, and estimated gross margin calculations using supplied SKU data.
actual_capabilities: Collect SKU names, quantities, reorder thresholds, unit costs, selling prices, and optional supplier notes.
Check that quantities are non-negative and prices and costs use matching currencies and units.
Flag stock at or below supplied reorder thresholds and prioritize replenishment candidates with stated assumptions.
Calculate estimated inventory cost value as on-hand quantity multiplied by unit cost.
Calculate gross margin amount and gross margin percentage when selling price is greater than zero.
Provide a CSV-ready inventory summary on request.
limitations: Requires manually entered data; no ecommerce, accounting, supplier, or purchase-order integration is provided.
Does not invent supplier lead times or demand forecasts.
Calculations exclude tax, shipping, refunds, discounts, shrinkage, and payment fees unless those inputs are supplied.
Provides operational estimates, not accounting or financial advice.

use_cases.title: Review weekly replenishment needs
use_cases.description: Identify SKUs at or below their reorder thresholds before preparing a replenishment list.

use_cases.title: Review inventory cost exposure
use_cases.description: Estimate the cost value of stock on hand and compare gross margins across products.

use_cases.title: Prepare a spreadsheet summary
use_cases.description: Check manually maintained SKU records and request a CSV-ready summary for operational review.

prompt_templates.title: Check one SKU
prompt_templates.prompt: Review SKU [name]: quantity [quantity], reorder threshold [threshold], unit cost [cost], and selling price [price], all in [currency]. Flag low stock and estimate gross margin.

prompt_templates.title: Review an inventory list
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these manually entered inventory records: [records]. Check non-negative quantities and consistent currencies and units. Flag stock at or below each supplied reorder threshold.

prompt_templates.title: Compare stock value and margins
prompt_templates.prompt: Using [inventory records], calculate inventory cost value, unit gross margin, and gross margin percentage for each SKU. Identify missing inputs and avoid percentage calculations for zero selling prices.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: compare inventory exposure and estimated margins.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a prioritized reorder review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [inventory records] and [supplier notes]. Prioritize reorder candidates using supplied thresholds and explain your assumptions. Do not invent demand forecasts or lead times. Provide a CSV-ready summary with stock status, inventory cost value, and estimated gross margins.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: combine validation, prioritization, and spreadsheet preparation.

output_examples.input: Review Mug-A: 8 units on hand, reorder threshold 10, unit cost USD 4, selling price USD 10.
output: Mug-A: low stock because 8 units is at or below the threshold of 10.
Estimated gross margin per unit: USD 6; gross margin percentage: 60%.
Reorder candidate; demand and supplier lead time were not supplied.

output_examples.input: Compare Pen-A and Notebook-B in USD. Pen-A has quantity 0, threshold 5, cost 1, and price 0. Notebook-B has quantity 20, threshold 10, cost 3, and price 5.
output: Pen-A: low stock; estimated inventory cost value USD 0; unit gross margin negative USD 1.
Pen-A: gross margin percentage not calculated because selling price is zero.
Notebook-B: above reorder threshold; estimated inventory cost value USD 60; unit gross margin USD 2; gross margin percentage 40%.
Review Pen-A first because it has no stock and is below its supplied threshold.

best_practices: Supply current on-hand quantities and an explicit reorder threshold for every SKU.
Use consistent currencies and units for costs and selling prices.
Verify estimates against source records and state any additional costs before making replenishment decisions.
anti_patterns: Treating the skill as a live inventory synchronization or automatic purchasing system.
Mixing currencies or package sizes without supplying conversion details.
Using estimated gross margin as net profit or relying on invented demand forecasts.

faq.question: Does StockPulse connect to my store or suppliers?
faq.answer: No. The workflow uses manually entered records and provides no store, supplier, accounting, or purchase-order connections.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide SKU or name, on-hand quantity, reorder threshold, unit cost, and selling price. Include supplier notes when relevant.

faq.question: When is a product flagged as low stock?
faq.answer: A product is flagged when its on-hand quantity is at or below the reorder threshold you supply.

faq.question: How is gross margin calculated?
faq.answer: Unit gross margin is selling price minus unit cost. Gross margin percentage divides that difference by selling price when the price exceeds zero.

faq.question: Are shipping, taxes, and payment fees included?
faq.answer: These costs are excluded unless you explicitly supply them. The results are operational estimates, not accounting or financial advice.

faq.question: Can I request spreadsheet output?
faq.answer: Yes. Request a CSV-ready summary of your supplied inventory data and the calculated estimates.
